messages:
maria (eng-runtime): Heads up — saw a steady RSS increase on Dedicated when running long-context chat sims (~60k tokens). Hosted and Private don't show the same slope. Anyone else seen this?

sam (eng-ml): Hmm, can you paste the perf profile? rough numbers fine.

maria (eng-runtime): Sure, quick summary: Dedicated GPU tasks show KV page growth from ~8.2GB -> 13.1GB over 45m of sustained traffic. Hosted stays ~8.4GB, Private ~8.9GB. Eviction rate on Dedicated is much lower (we're not reclaiming small slices).

maria (eng-runtime): Profiling hints: chunked-allocator still uses 4KB base pages, but page-frame compaction runs less frequently on Dedicated; stack shows occasional fallback to `cpu_kv_compact()` path (slow).

perf-bot: Perf run report: https://perf.redwood/reports/1830123456-kv-dedicated-growth — allocation flamegraph + GC events attached. :mag_right:

jordan (eng-infra): Could this be MTU / NIC offload differences in our Dedicated pools vs Hosted? RDMA/peer-memory differences can affect hugepage behavior. Dedicated hosts are using 9k MTU and different hugepage config.

maria (eng-runtime): Good call — I toggled hugepages on a repro node: enabling 2MB hugepages reduced fragmentation and forced larger frames; RSS growth stabilized but eviction latency increased 30ms. Tradeoff.

lee (eng-sre): Any VPC constraints for Private that could explain parity with Hosted? Private is VPC but customer-managed — we saw earlier that some VPC setups disallow guest hugepage allocation when nested virtualization present.

maria (eng-runtime): Right — Private nodes in our test had KVM flags off so kernel could use transparent hugepages; Dedicated cloud image had a kernel param `no_tscale` that prevented compaction in tight loops. Saw this in dmesg: "compact_memory: skipping due to policyX"

sam (eng-ml): Also, batching heuristics matter. When batch size bumps to 32 on Dedicated we fill more unique KV keys per batch (less reuse), so memory working set increases even before fragmentation. Did you compare same traffic shape?

maria (eng-runtime): Yes same workload generator. But Dedicated has slightly different kernel selection for attention kernels (we use kernel-v2 on Hosted, kernel-v1 fallback on Dedicated for some ops). That changes token emission pacing and KV footprint interleaving.

jordan (eng-infra): Actionable list from infra side:
- check kernel cmdline for `compact_memory` flags on Dedicated images
- align hugepage config with Hosted (or make runtime resilient)
- test MTU/offsloads flip on a canary node

maria (eng-runtime): From runtime side I'm going to: 
- instrument KV page allocator to emit per-frame age histogram
- add a periodic compaction pass when avg page age > threshold
- ensure we never hit the `cpu_kv_compact()` slow path by guarding allocation with fast-path checks

lee (eng-sre): Small repro steps would help. If you can drop a short script that reproduces on a single Dedicated GPU node that'd speed testing.

maria (eng-runtime): I'll push a tiny harness to ci/perf-repros and post link. Quick config snippet I'm testing now:

```yaml
runtime:
  kv:
    page_size: 2097152  # 2MB on repro node
    compaction_interval_s: 60
    reclaim_threshold: 0.7
batching:
  max_batch: 16
  dynamic_reuse_window: 128
```

sam (eng-ml): Try setting `max_batch` to 8 in Dedicated tests — might surface reuse benefits. Also collect KV hit/miss ratio per request id.

maria (eng-runtime): Will do. One more weirdness: when we forced the Dedicated node to use kernel-v2 for attention (same as Hosted) RSS growth pattern matched Hosted, but latency percentile spiked 5-10ms. So kernel selection + memory compaction interact.

jordan (eng-infra): We should avoid divergent defaults across fleets. I'll open an infra ticket to sync kernel cmdline and hugepage defaults between Hosted/Dedicated images.

maria (eng-runtime): Filed https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFRA-912 (link) to track. Will post perf harness and logs shortly. Thanks all. :pray:
